rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Section headers use command verbs when section is about doing something.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Re-derived against every ## in body: line 17 "Set the two return markers" (Set), line 28 "Pin the starting point" (Pin), line 37 "Push it only if you want it off this laptop" (Push), line 45 "Send it off" (Send), line 53 "Nudge sparingly while it runs" (Nudge). All five lead with a command verb; the section's body is about doing (keep laptop awake, nudge by hand, stop the run), so the verb-header test applies and is met. The adverb "sparingly" sits after the lead verb, so it does not reintroduce a noun-phrase-first header; it does not violate any other rule either (not a banned word, not a hedge, not a false claim — see check_writing.md rule 18, PASS above, on why "sparingly" is accurate to the section's dosage doctrine).
